builder_plan.scenario: Tool errors or unavailable services cause your agent to abandon recoverable tasks.
builder_plan.change: Inject repeatable tool failures and change only the recovery policy.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current retry and fallback behavior under the same injected failures.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Recovered tasks, duplicate side effects, retries, time to recovery, and total cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: HookEvo: A Framework for Coordinated Plugin Evolution on Hook-Enabled Agent Runtimes
summary: HookEvo replaces manual, one-off prompt and tool-glue fixes with an iterative loop in which an external improver model diagnoses execution traces and edits harness plugins (receipt interpretation, context assembly, action checks) through runtime lifecycle hooks. It costs repeated evaluation rounds on matched task suites plus API calls to a strong improver model, and it depends on a hook-enabled runtime such as DeepSeek Harness, adding harness code that must be maintained. It can fail when the evolved harness overfits to the evaluation tasks, when the improver introduces regressions that the retained-version check misses, or when the executor model or task distribution changes and the evolved plugins no longer transfer.
rationale: The method improves a frozen small model's agent performance without retraining, but it requires an existing hook-enabled runtime, matched evaluation tasks, and repeated improver API calls, so its benefit must be validated on the reader's own workload before adoption.
technique: Hook-based evolutionary repair of agent harnesses

claims.statement: HookEvo replaces manual, one-off prompt and tool-glue fixes with an iterative loop in which an external improver model diagnoses execution traces and edits harness plugins (receipt interpretation, context assembly, action checks) through runtime lifecycle hooks. It costs repeated evaluation rounds on matched task suites plus API calls to a strong improver model, and it depends on a hook-enabled runtime such as DeepSeek Harness, adding harness code that must be maintained. It can fail when the evolved harness overfits to the evaluation tasks, when the improver introduces regressions that the retained-version check misses, or when the executor model or task distribution changes and the evolved plugins no longer transfer.

With a frozen Qwen3-4B executor, evolved harnesses reach 95.41% on ALFWorld, 70.56% on DBBench, 48.17% on WebShop, and 41.67% on OSBench, leading the reported Qwen3-4B comparisons; coordinated executable edits give the largest average gain.
